page: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the cost-conscious General Purpose tier. It provides two vCPUs mapped to a fractional allocation of a single physical core on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, 16 MB of L3 cache, and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per allocated vCPU. The instance contains no dedicated hardware GPUs, includes no bundled local storage, and provides no complimentary IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the constraints imposed by fractional CPU scheduling and memory throughput limits. While single-core compute performance achieves intermediate levels in stress-ng at 2,642.19, multi-core stress-ng registers almost identically at 2,642.78, reflecting the shared fractional physical core ceiling. Geekbench scores remain modest at 661 for single-core and 682 for multi-core execution. Memory bandwidth reaches 39.35 GB/sec for small cached blocks, declining to 6.36 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 4.83 GB/sec for writes. PassMark metrics reflect these limitations, with a CPU score of 3,105.59, a memory score of 817.13, and database operations scoring 884.33. Service-level measurements indicate 0.82 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.63 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The qualitative profile of e2-medium prioritizes resource economy over sustained computational density. The architecture delivers cost-effective baseline compute for intermittent tasks, lightweight background services, microservices, development sandboxes, and low-traffic web endpoints. However, it is not suitable for continuous high-load operations, large databases, or intensive multi-threaded batch jobs due to shared physical core throttling and modest memory bandwidth.
description: Google Cloud Platform e2-medium is a shared-core general-purpose virtual machine designed for entry-level and intermittent workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.2 GHz, it provisions two vCPUs backed by a shared fractional physical core alongside 4.0 GB of RAM. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark assessments, e2-medium demonstrates average single-thread performance with a stress-ng score of 2,642.19, but multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations remain constrained by shared CPU time-slicing and uncached memory bandwidth of 6.36 GB/sec. Synthetic evaluations show a PassMark CPU score of 3,105.59 and Redis throughput of 0.82 million SET operations per second. With an architecture optimized for minimal baseline resource utilization, e2-medium serves development environments, internal utilities, lightweight microservices, and modest web servers that do not demand sustained compute cycles.
